title: Stone Points From Arabia May Have Carried Poison
paragraphs: About 125,000 years ago, a freshwater lake lay in what is now the Empty Quarter desert of Saudi Arabia. A team from Griffith University, King Abdullah University of Science and Technology and the Saudi Heritage Commission studied a site on its shore called 'Uruq Aljelibah. Their paper is in the journal Science.

The researchers recovered more than 5,000 stone tools beside fossils of animals such as hippos, buffalo, camels, gazelles and oryx. Under the microscope, some stone points showed animal tissue near the tip and plant resin and fibres at the base, which suggests they were fixed to shafts. Lead researcher Christopher Clarkson said this suggests people "were manufacturing composite weapons made from multiple materials".

Several points also carried chemical traces linked to a tree used for arrow poison. However, the team only says poison may have been used. The release gives no exact numbers, so it is hard to judge how strong the evidence is, and more research is needed.

questions.q: What did the microscope show at the base of the points?
Which animals lived near the lake?
questions.a: For example hippos, buffalo, camels, gazelles and oryx.

questions.q: How sure are the researchers about poison?
